entry_state: Payment defaults, remedies and succession need dated contractual events. Loan creation differs from external cash settlement; allowance populations and prudential capital differ from accounting totals. The synthetic bank now begins a rule-bounded allowance and exposure reconciliation.
exit_state: Allowance admission uses the pre-excess base; adequate capital does not pay an unfunded obligation. The dated loss model retains exposure-severity dependence. Asset classification must establish contractual cash flows and business model before the coming amortised-cost examples.
findings: The restricted prudential example distinguishes equity 23.6, CET1 21.6, admitted allowance 1.5, total capital 23.1 and final RWA 119.1. Its cap does not use its own reduced denominator.
The payment failure leaves 9 unpaid without changing the stated capital ratios. Missing average assets blocks leverage alone, not the supported risk-based ratios.
The richer loss expression retains the conditional product expectation and distinguishes eligible default times from later cash shortfalls.
Classification introduces cash-flow eligibility and business model before amortised-cost calculation; management intention for one asset is insufficient. No new defect observed.
